slides.title: More enquiries isn't the goal. [Better-fit work] is.
slides.lede: Accountancy firm branding should start with the clients you want to serve. It cannot begin with a discussion about colours or a new logo.

slides.title: Decide which [work] the partners want more of
slides.note: Assess each service against the direction you want. **Payroll** might be strategically important for one practice and use up advisory capacity in another.

items.title: Business stage
items.text: Start-up, established SME, expanding group or corporate?

items.title: Sector
items.text: Which industries can you genuinely serve well?

items.title: Complexity
items.text: What financial, tax or reporting complexity suits the team?

items.title: Decision-maker
items.text: Owner-manager, finance director, CFO or board?

items.title: Commercial fit
items.text: Does the engagement justify the resources required?

cards.label: Appealing to everyone
cards.text: Every service listed, generic messaging, no clear commercial audience.

cards.label: Recording three categories
cards.text: Priority clients, acceptable clients, deprioritised enquiries. Then concentrate resources.

slides.title: Make expertise [visible] instead of relying on adjectives
slides.text: Show a named partner's qualifications, demonstrable experience in a defined industry and documented case studies with client permission. A homepage calling the team experienced and dedicated gives buyers nothing to assess.

slides.quote: Judge the brand against the work you want to win, not the number of people who fill in a contact form.
slides.text: Track qualified enquiries, proposal conversion, engagement mix and client retention. Website traffic alone is a poor indicator.

slides.title: The client portfolio is the real measure.
slides.lede: Accounting firm branding strategy: start with the clients you want. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
